name: Deloitte (US-India offices, USI)
overview: Deloitte US-India offices (USI) are Deloitte's offices in India that work for the US firm. They hire students through campus programs and through the National Level Assessment (NLA) for freshers. Deloitte says its assessment tests vary across business areas.
variation_note: Deloitte says assessment tests vary across business areas; NLA (Analyst Trainee) and campus Analyst drives use different patterns, and Deloitte India (not USI) practice areas have their own rounds.

roles.title: Analyst Trainee (National Level Assessment)
roles.description: Fresher role hired through Deloitte's National Level Assessment, open to engineering and other graduates. Joiners are registered as apprentices for the first year according to PrepInsta.

eligibility.text: BE/BTech, ME/MTech, Integrated MTech, MCA and others; 60%+; no active backlogs (NLA 2026 post)
1-year probation from joining, open to rotational shifts, registered as an apprentice under the Apprenticeship Act

roles.title: Analyst (USI campus drive, e.g. Technology / Business Technology Analyst)
roles.description: Campus role in USI technology teams; interviews focus on projects, SQL, basic DSA and scenario questions.

eligibility.text: No active backlogs and 60% or more aggregate (Aug 2024 campus drive)

stages.name: Application, screening and pre-placement talk
stages.what: You apply through your campus career centre or the USI jobs site, your profile is screened, and campus drives usually start with a pre-placement talk by the Deloitte team.

format.text: Steps: apply, assessment rounds, pre-placement talks, selection rounds, offer
Online profile with resume, transcript details and location preference; reviewed after the deadline
NLA: registration, resume-based screening, online assessment, online interview, final results

study: Note your grades in relevant courses
tips: Do not create more than one account
Take notes in the pre-placement talk; you can mention it in the interview
stages.before_next: Start timed mixed MCQ practice (English, aptitude, CS fundamentals).
stages.label: Official

stages.name: Online assessment: English + Aptitude + Computer fundamentals
stages.what: One online test (often on HirePro) with English, reasoning, quant and technical MCQs. The coding section is in the same sitting.

format.text: NLA: 90 min total, 65 MCQs + 2 coding, no negative marking: English 10 MCQs + 3 fill in the blanks, 12 reasoning + 10 quant, 30 computer fundamentals (testing, CS, networking and cybersecurity, cloud, chosen language)
NLA: 67 questions (65 MCQs + 2 coding) in 90 min shared
NLA (Feb 2025): HirePro, 90 min, 5 sections, 67 questions, no negative marking, free navigation between sections
NLA (2024): 20 aptitude, 10 English, 20 technical (debugging, programming concepts, testing, cloud, MS Office), 2 coding, 90 min
USI campus (Aug 2024): HirePro, 90 min; analytical, quant, verbal, CS fundamentals (OS, DBMS, cloud, SQL, pseudocode); about 49 of 300 shortlisted
Deloitte India campus (2025 batch): 50 questions in 60 min; quant and logical 20 in 25 min, verbal 10 in 10 min, computer fundamentals 20 in 25 min

study: Percentages, profit and loss, time and work
OS, DBMS, networks, cloud, software testing
tips: About 1 minute per question, so do not get stuck
No negative marking in NLA reports, so attempt everything
Keep pen and paper for calculations
stages.before_next: Do one full 90-minute mock with all sections.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Online assessment: Coding section
stages.what: Two coding problems in the same test, usually one string and one array problem, in a language you choose.

format.text: 1 live coding task + 1 live programming question; C, C++, C#, Java, Python and others; hidden test cases shown after Compile & Execute
2 coding questions, one on strings and one on arrays, easy to moderate
2 problems (1 easy, 1 medium), about 20 min kept for coding
2 easy coding questions
Online assessment had 1 SQL query and 1 easy coding question (Aug 2023 BTA drive)

study: Basic SQL SELECT with WHERE and JOIN
tips: Use Compile & Execute and fix failing cases before final submit
stages.before_next: Practise 10 easy string and array problems in your language.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Versant (spoken English) test, some drives
stages.what: An automated spoken English test reported in some campus drives as a separate elimination round.

format.text: Online assessment followed by a Versant test; both elimination rounds (Aug 2023 campus drive)

tips: Use a quiet room and speak at a steady pace
stages.before_next: Prepare your self-introduction and project pitch.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Technical + HR interview
stages.what: An interview on your projects, programming basics, SQL and scenario questions. Some interviewers focus on HR, others on technical topics.

format.text: NLA: single round of about 15 to 25 min with technical and HR questions
NLA (Feb 2025): online video interview, about 30 to 40 min, with live coding
USI campus: one-on-one, 30 to 50 min after the pre-placement talk
NLA (2024): about 40 min
BTA campus: technical round about 45 min

tips: Explain why you chose your tech stack
Give brute force first, then the better solution
Be honest about what you know
stages.before_next: Prepare stories for teamwork, deadlines and handling pressure.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

stages.name: Managerial / partner round, some roles
stages.what: Some drives add a second interview with a manager, director or partner that goes deeper into projects and workplace scenarios. Some Deloitte India practice areas also hold a group discussion before it.

format.text: BTA campus: managerial round about 45 min with deep project questions and scenario questions
Deloitte India ADMM (2025 batch): group discussion, director interview, then partner round with HR and scenario questions

study: Database migration and concurrency basics for your project
Current tech topics like Gen AI
tips: Stay calm if interrupted; it can be a composure test
Have a question ready for the interviewer
stages.before_next: Keep documents ready; results are often shared through your college within a day or two.
stages.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Find the missing number in an array containing numbers from 1 to N with one number missing. Give time and space complexity.
questions.answer: Missing = N*(N+1)/2 minus sum of the array. [1,2,4,5,6] with N=6 gives 3. O(n) time, O(1) space.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: How would you handle a situation where a project is cancelled close to the deadline?
questions.answer: Stay calm, understand why, save and document the work done, move the team to the new priority, and note what can be reused.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: OOP
questions.question: Explain inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation and abstraction.
questions.answer: Inheritance: reuse a parent class. Polymorphism: one name, many forms (overloading/overriding). Encapsulation: hide data behind methods. Abstraction: show only what is needed.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Write a program to print the characters of a string with their ASCII codes.
questions.answer: for ch in s: print(ch, ord(ch)). 'AB' prints A 65 and B 66.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is Arduino and what is it used for?
questions.answer: A low-cost open-source microcontroller board you program to read sensors and control devices; used in IoT, robotics and prototypes.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Print an inverted full pyramid star pattern in Python.
questions.answer: for i in range(n,0,-1): print(' '*(n-i) + '*'*(2*i-1)). For n=4 the rows have 7, 5, 3, 1 stars.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Coding
questions.question: Sort a random array of integers. Explain bubble sort and merge sort with their time complexity.
questions.answer: Bubble sort swaps neighbours: O(n^2) worst/average. Merge sort splits, sorts and merges: O(n log n) always, O(n) extra space.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: What is the marquee tag in HTML, and what are the advantages of Bootstrap?
questions.answer: <marquee> scrolls text but is obsolete (use CSS animation). Bootstrap gives a ready responsive grid and components, so pages build faster and look consistent.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: HR
questions.question: A colleague is stuck and their deadline is very close, but your team's deadline is also close. How will you help?
questions.answer: Check the size of their issue, give quick focused help or point to the right person, keep your own commitment, and tell your lead early if timelines are at risk.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Project
questions.question: Suggest improvements for an autonomous parking system.
questions.answer: Example points: better sensors and camera fusion, live slot availability in an app, pre-booking and payments, safety fallbacks, and logging data to improve the model.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Group discussion: an EV company has good sales but poor after-sales service and little digitalisation, so customers are unhappy. Propose a solution.
questions.answer: Possible points: service booking app with tracking, connected-car diagnostics, more trained service partners, feedback loops and clear service SLAs.
questions.label: Candidate-reported

questions.subject: Pseudocode
questions.question: What is printed? x=5, y=0; for i = 1 to x: if i mod 2 == 0 then y = y + i else y = y - 1; print y
questions.answer: 3. Odd i (1,3,5) subtract 1 each (-3), even i add 2 + 4 (+6), so y = 3.
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Quant
questions.question: A can finish a job in 12 days and B in 18 days. How many days do they take together?
questions.label: AI practice

questions.subject: Other
questions.question: Which type of testing checks that a new change has not broken existing features?
questions.answer: Regression testing re-runs existing tests after a change.
questions.label: AI practice
